citations.claim: Pole angle exceeded 0.8 rad limit at first violating step, with theta -0.897 rad
One step before violation pole was still within limit
Two steps before violation pole was within limit, showing rapid divergence

explanation: Seeded sensor noise (0.02) with coarse dt=0.02 and initial offset x=0.5,v=0.5,theta=0.1 causes state-feedback controller to apply wrong-direction/lagging forces; pole angular rate grows to ~-6.2 rad/s by step 13 and angle diverges past 0.8 rad at step 14. Likely cause is noise-corrupted feedback combined with large control step destabilizing the upright equilibrium.
vision_note: The cart stays near the center of the track from steps 11 to 13 while the pole leans progressively farther to the left. At step 14 the pole tip turns red, indicating the pole angle has exceeded the upright limit.
